data.name: Rodi
data.gender_notes: Rodi is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word ‘ροδί’ (rhodi), which means ‘red.’ This name has biblical roots as it is mentioned in the New Testament as the name of the island where Saint Paul was held captive and ministered to the inhabitants. The name Rodi carries the meaning “Red” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Rodi usually hope their child will grow to embody red and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes passion, courage, and resilience in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Rodi belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Red.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rodi total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rodi was historically used for locations and individuals, with the island of Rhodes famously known for its ancient ruins, including the Colossus of Rhodes, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World. It was also known for its strategic location and commercial prosperity. This cultural impact suggests strength, resilience, and a sense of pride in one's history and heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Rodi holds spiritual significance as it is associated with the apostle Paul's captivity and ministry on the Island of Rhodes. As per the Acts of the Apostles (27:39-44), during his imprisonment, Paul healed the slave, Publius, and the entire island was saved from a severe illness. This event showcases how even in the midst of captivity, an individual can make a positive impact on the lives of others. Furthermore, Rhodes is known in Greek mythology as the birthplace of Helios (God of the Sun). This spiritual connection seeks to shine a light on the name Rodi, representing hope, healing, and a connection to the divine.
